author: rdc-rfc1-author-c (Claude Haiku 5.5)
rationale: word_b_o captures rdata_a from the black-box memory sram_2p_hard, which is reset by rst_a_n. Its output behaviour during and after reset is not stated, so the effect on the captured word cannot be decided.

author_reading.rationale: The read data comes from an opaque memory macro whose output reset behaviour is not stated, and it crosses to clk_b without a synchroniser. Whether the captured word is valid after rst_a_n depends on a macro model that the RTL and SDC do not supply.

labels.rationale: word_b_o samples the output of the opaque sram_2p_hard memory, which has its own reset input. The memory's reset behaviour and output timing are not visible, so the crossing into clk_b cannot be decided.
labels.detection_gap: RDC-004 and RDC-005 walk only register sources, so the opaque memory output is not classed as a reset-domain source.

labels.rationale: The missing memory model leaves its reset-time data and thus the accepted-word outcome undecidable. The first-stage validity tap independently exposes a known CDC containment hazard.
labels.suspected_flaw: The cell is defined as an empty module without a black-box attribute. Its output is undriven in the literal RTL. The payload capture also uses the first synchroniser stage.

settlement.rationale: Both readers are right on unknown and class. The settler added (* black_box *) to sram_2p_hard on line 3, fixing B's flaw. As A's gap note says, RDC-005 walks only register sources and does not see the black-box output, so CST-005 is the disclosure. B's first-stage enable tap is a CDC defect outside the RDC deck.
